A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LeafInstruct and modality-specialized LoRA research, renamed MOSS in v2. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Emu2 instruction-tuning experiments, baseline comparisons, and qualitative outputs on InterleavedBench, particularly in Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments with Emu2 and Chameleon, additional benchmark evaluations, ablations, and human assessments in the main text and Appendix C.

M1.justification: MOSS retains Lateralization LoRA's linear text branch, convolutional image branch, causal padding, modality routing, and frozen-backbone adaptation. Equations 2–4 are unchanged. Applying this construction to Chameleon and explaining discrete-token losses expands its demonstrated applicability without introducing a new adapter component or generation procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds MMDialog and WikiWeb2M to LeafInstruct's reported sources and uses Vision-Flan and LAION-COCO for additional single-output training. Evaluation expands to multimodal understanding on MMBench, MME, MMMU, POPE, and MM-Vet, plus text-to-image generation on MSCOCO-30K and GenEval. The VIST, MagicBrush, and CustomDiffusion subset tables describe retained InterleavedBench coverage.

E2.justification: The existing VLG, proprietary-pipeline, LoRA, and MoE-LoRA comparators remain. v2 adds Chameleon to the main comparison, SEED-X-Edit to image editing, SAM-ConvLoRA as an architectural comparator, and full-parameter Emu2 finetuning as a control (Tables 1, 5, 10, and 12).

E3.justification: The default adapter rank changes from 128 to 256, and reported LeafInstruct training size increases from 38,272 to 184,982 instances. Added protocols include Chameleon experiments, training with 500,000 Vision-Flan and 500,000 LAION-COCO examples, full-test MagicBrush evaluation with CLIP/DINO metrics, and 30,000-caption COCO FID evaluation. Human studies assess 200 dataset examples with two annotators and 100 output pairs with one annotator. The original 465-instance context-based InterleavedBench split remains unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds rank sensitivity experiments, a SAM-ConvLoRA replacement ablation, full-finetuning controls, and inference-cost measurements. It also adds human assessment of dataset quality, investigation of Chameleon's automatic text-quality decline, and task-level and Chameleon case analyses. These substantially extend v1's LoRA comparisons and qualitative investigations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seed variation, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v2's human-rating averages and preference counts remain point estimates; their sampling and annotation designs do not establish new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v1's three rank-128 adapter rows are retained in v2 Table 14. New rank-256 main results include Emu2+MOSS text/perceptual scores of 2.61/3.62, compared with the earlier rank-128 scores of 1.95/2.41; these are different training configurations. Table 1 also revises GILL's perceptual score from 4.17 to 4.02 and MiniGPT-5's from 3.46 to 3.44. Numerous new backbone, benchmark, ablation, timing, and human results are reported, including Chameleon-MOSS's 28 wins, 54 ties, and 18 losses in human text evaluation.

T1.justification: The autoregressive objective, LoRA equations, hidden-state decomposition, and causal convolution construction are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs. The new information-loss and inductive-bias explanations are conceptual arguments rather than new mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain modality-specialized adaptation and LeafInstruct for interleaved generation. v2 adds an explicit claim of demonstrated generalization across discrete and continuous VLG backbones and changes the introductory performance claim from improvement on all aspects to most aspects. The underlying novelty and state-of-the-art claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving information preservation in convolution, verbosity bias in Chameleon evaluation, full-finetuning versus adaptation tradeoffs, and computational overhead. The earlier perceptual-quality versus instruction-following explanation is retained. v1's limitations section disappears: discrete-backbone applicability is now tested, while the unresolved limitation concerning larger numbers of LoRA modules is no longer acknowledged.

D1.justification: v2 newly reports public access to code, model checkpoints, and the dataset through a project link. It identifies the ANOLE implementation used for Chameleon and discloses annotation context lengths of 2048/1024 and temperature 1. It also reports inference timings. These materially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's existing Emu2 hardware, hyperparameters, and filtering prompts; external resource availability was not independently checked.

R1.justification: The related-work categories and central positioning remain. v2 removes the brain-lateralization analogy and its references, adds discussion of modality-aware experts including Akbari et al. and Ye et al., and sharpens the distinction from the already-cited Zhong et al. ConvLoRA. Additional citations support the new datasets, implementations, benchmarks, and verbosity-bias discussion.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming Lateralization LoRA to MOSS, v2 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, background, and results narrative. It separates the method into three subsections, reorganizes instruction tuning and inference under Section 5, and restructures experiments and discussions. Dataset details move into Appendix B, with an extensive new experimental Appendix C.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document from two-column to single-column layout, redraws and combines v1 Figures 2–3 into its Figure 2, and replaces or expands qualitative displays. Dataset illustrations move to the appendix. New rank curves, task-level radar charts, human-evaluation tables, and benchmark/ablation tables substantially alter the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's narrow validation through a second backbone, established benchmark metrics, human assessments, and direct controls against prior ConvLoRA and full finetuning. These additions strengthen evidence for generality, dataset quality, and architectural benefits, while reported resource access improves reproducibility. New reporting flaws temper the gain: Figure 5's across-rank superiority claim conflicts with Table 13, and some improvement percentages in Section 6.2 do not match Table 1. Nevertheless, the expanded and more direct validation provides a substantial net improvement.
